in_arabic.name: كاروبة

in_pashto.name: کاروبه
in_pashto.long_meaning: کاروبه د مؤنثو نومونو څخه دی چې په پښتو کې کارول کیږي. دا نوم د عربي ژبې څخه اخیستل شوی دی او معنی یې ده نږدې يا ګرانه. په افغانستان او پاکستان کې د پښتنو په منځ کې دا نوم د هغو کسانو لپاره کارول کېږي چې د زړه سره نږدې وي.

data.cultural_impact: In various Muslim communities, the name "Karoobah" is Aberrationally given to infants born during the holy month of Ramadan. The naming convention is thought to have originated from the story of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) and how he led his family on a long journey with their camels during the scorching heat. During this journey, Hagar, Ibrahim's wife, was desperate for water for her infant son Ismail (Ishmael), who was also a namesake for children born during Ramadan. Eventually, God sent a miracle in the form of a gushing well from beneath the foot of Ismail's camel. This exemplifies the time-honored traditions and beliefs of the nomadic Muslim communities who have a deep connection with camels as essential companions for long, arduous journeys across desert landscapes.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Karoobah" possesses spiritual significance as it's symbolic of the strength, endurance and resilience that Muslims are encouraged to display during the holy month of Ramadan. Like a baby camel, a newborn Muslim is believed to embark on a spiritual journey that calls for them to adapt to the discipline and hardships faced during the month. The name also serves as a reminder of God's Providence and mercy, as illustrated in the story of Hagar and Ismail, when God intervened by sending water to quench their thirst. Through the enduring spirit embodied by the name "Karoobah," the community imparts inspiring messages of trust, perseverance and devotion to God.
